Which parameters also explain the data?

These are sampled sensitivity ranges, not confidence intervals. Candidates within the stated MSE tolerance of the conventional fit are included; ranges depend on the search domain, grid, noise, and known sine-wave model. A narrow range does not certify the assumptions.

Inspect the measurements used for fitting

Both networks and the conventional fit receive exactly these observations. The clean initial profile is also known to all methods.

Three genuinely different methods

Data-only NN: learns the field from observations plus 32 known initial-condition points. It has no equation loss and makes no speed or diffusion estimate.

Inverse PINN: same network, initialization, data and training budget, plus a transport residual at 32 sampled points per step. It jointly learns v and log D. Objective: data MSE + initial MSE + 0.1 × equation MSE. Periodicity is built into both networks; mass conservation is checked, not enforced.

Conventional fit: grid search and local refinement fit the exact sine-wave solution to observations. This stronger solution-family prior makes it a useful reference. It is not a neural network or a finite-volume solver.

A model you can keep

Each run trains fresh neural weights for one experiment. Download them as JSON and use predictModel from the public repository for inference without retraining. This is not yet one pretrained model that generalizes across experiments.

Forecast RMSE uses unseen times t > 0.4. The hidden solution is used for generating observations and scoring only. Synthetic truth is inspectable in the browser; this is a scientific benchmark, not a secure guessing game.

With measurements only at t = 0, neither speed nor diffusion can be identified. The networks may still return numbers; the lab marks them as unsupported. Try several seeds and noise levels before drawing conclusions.
